title: Flow-Based Lattice Surgery Optimization with Runtime T Gate Scheduling
authors: Raymond Iacobacci, Tianyi Hao, Neer Patel, Siyuan Niu
abstract: Lattice surgery on the surface code is a leading route to fault-tolerant quantum computation. Compiling logical circuits into lattice surgery operations is a pivotal step that determines the resource cost of a computation. Prior compilers build on idealized assumptions, and one that works in practical settings remains to be developed. Existing works are either unscalable or route one gate at a time within a layer, so the embedding depends on the order of gates and opportunities to route many gates at once are lost. In addition, they assume magic states are always available and cost-free, even though preparing one costs more than a Clifford operation.   We present FlowRouter, the first topological lattice surgery compiler that places Clifford routing and stochastic magic state cultivation inside a single 3D embedding. At compile time, FlowRouter formulates the routing of an entire circuit layer as a maximum-flow problem, embedding many gates simultaneously. At runtime, it allows magic states to be cultivated at every idling patch, works with the realistic cultivation process with multiplexing and multi-stage post-selections, and absorbs the stochasticity by introducing delay mechanisms that add as little spacetime volume as possible. With magic states assumed free, FlowRouter reduces spacetime volume by 2.3x and compiles 10.8x faster than the state-of-the-art static topological lattice surgery compiler. With the cultivation-aware setting that includes both Clifford and magic state cost, FlowRouter reduces spacetime volume by 2.3x on a distance-13 surface code when compared with the state-of-the-art runtime compiler.
summary: This paper introduces FlowRouter, a novel compiler for lattice surgery on the surface code designed to optimize resource usage for fault-tolerant quantum computation. It treats Clifford gate routing and magic state cultivation simultaneously within a 3D embedding, solving the entire layer's routing via a max-flow formulation. This approach yields substantial reductions in required spacetime volume and improves compilation speed over existing state-of-the-art methods.
main_problem: Developing a practical, scalable compiler for lattice surgery on the surface code to minimize the resource cost (spacetime volume) of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: The proposed FlowRouter compiler significantly reduces spacetime volume (by 2.3x) and compilation time compared to state-of-the-art methods, even when accounting for realistic magic state cultivation costs.
method: It formulates the routing of an entire circuit layer as a maximum-flow problem at compile time, while handling stochastic magic state cultivation (MSC) at runtime within a single 3D embedding.
model_or_system: The system is fault-tolerant quantum computation implemented via lattice surgery on the surface code. The process is modeled using 3D topological pipe diagrams derived from ZX diagrams.
key_observables: Spacetime volume (resource cost), circuit fidelity, and compilation time.
important_parameters: Surface code distance (e.g., distance-13), Clifford and T gate costs, and magic state cultivation parameters.
main_assumptions: The compiler jointly handles Clifford routing and stochastic magic state cultivation, which previously were treated separately or assumed free.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process flow from input circuits to 3D pipe diagrams, showing the realization of the {H, S, CX, T} gate set and comparing performance metrics.
paper_structure: The paper introduces FlowRouter, detailing its compile-time max-flow approach for layer routing and its runtime mechanism for magic state cultivation, comparing its performance against existing static and runtime compilers.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum computation, the optimization techniques—especially the use of max-flow to solve complex resource allocation problems in a time-expanded graph—are relevant to resource management in any complex physical system.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
